title: Benchmark launches all-origin and non-China prices for six critical minerals delivered into the US
author: Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Benjamin Roche
text: Benchmark has launched two new sets of combined prices for praseodymium-neodymium (PrNd) oxide, dysprosium oxide, terbium oxide, yttrium oxide, gallium metal, and germanium metal, all assessed CIF North America. One set covers material of all origins; the other covers non-China origin only. Each grade combines contract and spot transactions, reflecting how these materials actually change hands in the North American market.The launch responds to policies that mean origin carries a cost. From 1 January 2027, the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) restriction on covered materials widens from where they are melted or produced to where they are mined, refined and separated, bringing the inputs to NdFeB and samarium-cobalt magnets under scrutiny throughout their supply chains. Gallium and germanium follow on 18 December 2027. In the meantime, China's pause on its expanded rare earth controls expires on 10 January, as will its suspension of the US export ban on gallium, germanium, and antimony on 27 January."From January, where a critical mineral comes from becomes a question of compliance and cost for US defence supply chains," said Daniel Fletcher-Manuel, Director of Indexing & Derivatives at Benchmark. "These grades make that cost visible, observed and comparable across six of the materials most exposed to Chinese export controls."Pricing compliant supplyUntil now, prices for these materials have not distinguished Chinese from non-Chinese supply. That has left defence contractors with no benchmark for showing that compliant material is available at a reasonable price, and policymakers with no observed reference for the price floors and border adjustments now being negotiated with allies.The non-China grade is defined to follow the logic of the DFARS rules: Taiwan-origin material is treated as Chinese origin, and recycled material processed outside China is treated as non-China origin. The difference between the two grades, the origin premium, varies widely from one element to another. In the first assessment on 26 November, it ranged from about 3% for terbium to 60% for yttrium, with PrNd at 4%, germanium at 7%, dysprosium at 10% and gallium at 16%. PrNd is the one element of the six that China does not control for export, and its premium has stayed within a few percentage points of zero through 2026. That makes it the clearest test of whether the DFARS changes alone will create a premium from January.
